applies_why: The judge text rules on D5 versus C5 by treating the sign's chapter-bound verses and the almah/bethulah word-count as the dispositive comparison, which is the chain-pressing situation K-C governs.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- the sign's chapter bounds (Isaiah 7:16; 8:3-4; 8:8) are real, but C5's own narrowing concedes Matthew 1:23's application stands, and the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways (Joel 1:8); answered in [CR2] section G and [CR3] LINK 5.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: 'weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse': I weighed whether this required comparing the pressed verses only as part of the whole pressing chain against C5's chain by footing, or allowed the judge to assess the sign's chapter bounds and the almah/bethulah word-count as individual verse/word evidence.
why: The judge calls D5 vs C5 underdetermined by weighing individual chapter-bound verses and the almah/bethulah word-count, not by weighing the pressed chain against C5's chain by footing as K-C requires.
